reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) concerns a CrMnFeNi HEA and 316H stainless steel in FLiBe salt at 700 °C, focusing on Mn dissolution and Cr retention. None of the passages address Q235 steel, its native iron oxide scale, its room-temperature behavior, or oxide spallation mechanisms. The premises about Q235 oxide stability and the reference behavior of 316L are therefore unsupported by the cited studies.
premises: Native iron oxide on Q235 is continuous and self-healing at room temperature
Native iron oxide becomes unstable and less adherent at 700–900 °C in molten salt
Oxide spallation permits accelerated salt penetration and rapid degradation
316L stainless steel maintains a protective oxide layer at high temperature
Mn dissolution in molten salt can influence corrosion behavior of alloys
